output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates a predominantly amnestic profile with multi-domain involvement. Episodic memory is severely impaired: RAVLT immediate recall at the 5th percentile, delayed recall at the 2nd percentile and recognition at the 4th percentile, consistent with a storage-type deficit. Semantic fluency (Category Fluency, Animals, 8th percentile) and confrontation naming (Boston Naming Test, 16th percentile) are below expected norms. Executive function (Trail Making B, 11th percentile) is reduced. Processing speed (Trail Making A, 25th percentile) and visuoconstructive ability (Rey Complex Figure Copy, 28th percentile) are at the lower limit of normal. Screening scores: MMSE 21/30, MoCA 15/30. Mood screening is within the normal range (GDS 4/15). Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 13 cmH2O. WBC 2 cells/uL (lymphocytes), RBC 0. Protein 44 mg/dL, glucose 59.8 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.64), all within reference ranges. Decreased Abeta42 (372 pg/mL) and Abeta42/40 ratio (0.046) with elevated p-tau181 (82 pg/mL) and total tau (520 pg/mL). This biomarker profile is consistent with Alzheimer disease pathology. Clinical correlation recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MMSE 21/30 with amnestic-predominant impairment not helped by cueing and informant-confirmed decline over two years; instrumental independence lost (finances taken over, household appliances and shopping), placing the syndrome at mild dementia
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive and behavioural assessment with informant history: a validated bedside instrument with the per-domain breakdown, whether delayed recall improves with cueing, and an explicit account of which instrumental activities have been lost. The syndrome must be documented before it is attributed
action_criteria.rationale: Whether this is mild cognitive impairment or dementia is decided clinically, by a validated instrument and her daughter's account of instrumental function, before any biomarker is interpreted [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic profile with disproportionate impairment of delayed recall and limited benefit from cueing, plus involvement of at least one other cognitive domain
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the cognitive profile and establish a baseline for tracking
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing defines the domains involved beyond the bedside screen, separates a storage-type memory deficit from the effect of bereavement and low mood, and sets a baseline for follow-up [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal TSH, B12 312 pg/mL with normal homocysteine and folate, non-reactive RPR and negative HIV, normal electrolytes and calcium: no reversible contributor
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid dysfunction, B12 deficiency, syphilis, HIV and electrolyte or calcium disturbance (she takes magnesium and calcium supplements) are treatable contributors that must be excluded before the decline is attributed to a neurodegenerative cause [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral hippocampal atrophy (Scheltens MTA 3 right, 2-3 left) with temporoparietal cortical volume loss; Fazekas grade 1 without infarct, hemorrhage or mass
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with dementia (volumetric) protocol to assess medial-temporal atrophy and exclude vascular disease, hippocampal sclerosis, NPH, and mass lesions
action_criteria.rationale: Structural MRI excludes vascular, mass and hydrocephalic causes of the decline and shows whether the atrophy pattern supports Alzheimer disease [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181 and total tau, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and it is needed when the diagnosis remains uncertain after the clinical, neuropsychological and MRI assessment or when disease-modifying treatment is being considered [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction needing a dose change; counselling on diarrhea with magnesium oxide, upper gastrointestinal effects with alendronate, weight loss at a BMI of 19.8, and vagotonic bradycardia
action_criteria.label: Check donepezil against her current medicines before starting it
action_criteria.rationale: A cholinesterase inhibitor is offered for mild Alzheimer dementia; magnesium oxide and alendronate add gastrointestinal effects in a woman with a BMI of 19.8, although none is a contraindication [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the decline to bereavement or loneliness; grief does not explain impaired recognition memory and the progressive loss of instrumental function.
Do not start memantine at the mild dementia stage; it is for moderate or severe Alzheimer disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97].

Do not add sedating or anticholinergic drugs (benzodiazepines, sedating antihistamines, tricyclics) for low mood or sleep; they worsen cognition and raise fall and fracture risk with her osteoporosis [Beers_2023].
required_recommendations: Disclose the diagnosis of mild Alzheimer dementia to her and her daughter, and discuss prognosis, advance care planning, durable power of attorney and carer support [NICE_NG97].

Assess whether she can keep living alone safely and arrange support at home: help with meals and food safety, appliances and shopping, supervision of her medicines, and a carer's assessment for her daughter; keep the finances with her daughter and protect her from scams.

Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines, monitoring weight closely because her BMI is 19.8 [NICE_NG97].

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].
Support nutrition, physical activity and social contact: dietary review for her low weight and proximal weakness, and a supported return to her walking group.
Continue blood pressure management (142/80 mmHg on amlodipine) as part of vascular risk care.

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardiac symptom or syncope to justify it in this case
Echocardiography is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardioembolic indication in this presentation
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; no arrhythmia, syncope, or palpitations described
Head CT adds little when MRI is available; MRI is the preferred structural modality for dementia workup

differential.key_features: No visual hallucinations, misidentification, fluctuations, dream enactment, tremor or rigidity; the cautious gait has no festination or freezing; amnestic storage-type profile with temporoparietal atrophy

No personality change, disinhibition, apathy out of proportion, compulsions or hyperorality, and no primary aphasia; amnestic profile with temporoparietal-predominant atrophy, and Alzheimer biomarkers when obtained
No significant cerebrovascular burden on MRI and the gradual amnestic course is not stepwise — pure VCI is unlikely

Mood has been somewhat low since bereavement four years ago, but she denies persistent sadness and anhedonia, GDS is 4/15, and recognition memory is impaired without cue benefit, which is not the pattern of depression-related cognitive impairment

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or sleep-related cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: TSH, B12 (312 pg/mL with normal homocysteine), folate, RPR, HIV, electrolytes and calcium are normal; sleep unchanged; the progressive amnestic decline is not explained by any of these

key_clinical_evidence: Probable Alzheimer disease dementia is a clinical diagnosis under NIA-AA 2011: insidious onset, informant-confirmed progression, an amnestic presentation with another domain affected, and decline in usual activities; hippocampal and temporoparietal atrophy on MRI support it but are not required [NIA_AA_2011]
The hallmark cognitive feature of AD is impaired delayed recall with rapid forgetting and limited benefit from cueing, reflecting a storage-type (hippocampal) memory deficit

Early decline is often put down to loneliness or grief in a widowed person living alone; progressive loss of instrumental function with impaired recognition memory calls for a dementia work-up and a safety plan
Cholinesterase inhibitors are indicated for mild to moderate Alzheimer dementia; memantine is for moderate or severe disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97]

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Yoshiko Mori is a 79-year-old right-handed retired florist who presents to the neurology outpatient clinic accompanied by her daughter, Keiko, for evaluation of progressive memory difficulties that have been worsening over the past two years. Her daughter first became concerned approximately two years ago when she noticed her mother was repeating the same questions within a single phone conversation, something that had never happened before. At first, the family attributed this to loneliness following her husband's death four years ago, but the pattern has steadily worsened. Over the past year, her daughter has discovered unpaid utility bills piled in a drawer, and on one occasion the electricity was briefly disconnected before the daughter intervened and began managing her mother's finances. Mrs. Mori, who ran a flower shop for 35 years and was known for elaborate ikebana arrangements, attempted to arrange flowers for a neighbor's memorial service six months ago but lost track of the sequence and abandoned the task, something her daughter describes as unprecedented. She has also stopped attending her weekly senior walking group, telling her daughter she cannot remember the meeting time despite having attended the same session for over five years. Her daughter reports that the refrigerator frequently contains expired food, and she has found the same grocery items purchased multiple times on the same day. Three months ago, Mrs. Mori called her daughter in distress because she could not remember how to operate the washing machine she has used for fifteen years. She remains able to dress herself, maintain personal hygiene, and prepare simple meals such as rice and miso soup, though her daughter notes the meals have become much less varied than before. Mrs. Mori acknowledges that her memory is not as sharp as it used to be and appears embarrassed when her daughter provides examples. She denies episodes of confusion where she did not recognize family members, visual hallucinations, personality changes, or aggressive behavior. She denies headaches, seizures, falls, tremor, or difficulty swallowing. Her sleep pattern has not significantly changed, and her daughter has not witnessed unusual movements or vocalizations during sleep. Her mood has been somewhat low since her husband's passing, but she denies persistent sadness, anhedonia, or suicidal ideation, and she still enjoys watching historical dramas on television.

neurological_exam.additional: No paratonic rigidity. No grasp reflex. No myoclonus. No primitive reflexes elicited. Anosmia not formally tested. Mild kyphotic posture.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin mildly unsteady bilaterally but no clear cerebellar pattern. Rapid alternating movements slightly slowed but symmetric.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Visual fields full to confrontation. Face symmetric. Hearing mildly reduced bilaterally, consistent with age-related presbycusis. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly cautious gait with normal base. Stride length slightly shortened. Tandem gait performed slowly but without significant deviation. Romberg negative. No festination, no freezing.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place. Oriented to month and year but states the date is off by five days. MMSE 21/30: lost 3 points on recall (0/3 at 5 minutes), 2 points on orientation (date and day of week), 1 point on serial sevens, 1 point on sentence writing (incomplete thought), 1 point on figure copy (slight distortion of intersecting pentagons), and 1 point on the three-stage command (omits the last step). Clock drawing shows all 12 numbers present but crowded on the right side, with hands placed at an incorrect time (asked for 2:45, drew approximately 3:00). Naming intact for common objects; hesitates on low-frequency items such as 'lapel' and 'buckle'. Repetition intact. Follows simple commands without difficulty but makes an error on a three-step command (omits the last step). Fluency mildly reduced on category testing (animals: 9 in 60 seconds).
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk mildly reduced in bilateral lower extremities consistent with age-related sarcopenia. Tone normal throughout. Strength 5/5 in upper extremities, 4+/5 in bilateral hip flexors, 5/5 distally in lower extremities. No pronator drift. No tremor or involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 1+ at biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis bilaterally. 1+ at patellar tendons bilaterally. Achilles reflexes trace bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick in all extremities. Vibration sense mildly diminished at bilateral great toes. Proprioception intact.
